title: Staged Update Digest + Rollback-Aware Customer Comms Kit
creator: Ethan Gold
description:
Summary:

This ticket delivers a reusable, customer-facing communications kit for staged upgrades across Redwood Inference deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). The key differentiator is explicit, rollback-aware messaging: every outbound touch includes the rollback window, automated canary observations customers can monitor, and guidance specific to channel (LTS vs rolling). The kit contains:

- A concise release digest template intended for email and the Console release notes pane.
- Segmented messaging templates (PLG self-serve customers, Dedicated reserved customers, Private/VPC customers).
- In-app banner and Console banner copy variations with timers and opt-out links.
- Pre-upgrade checklist and remediation runbook customers can attach to their internal tickets.
- A rollback-ready migration FAQ and a post-rollback incident summary template.

Goals:

1) Reduce support volume spikes during LTS rollouts by setting clear expectations and automated canary observability links.
2) Prevent surprise regressions by surfacing per-endpoint risk and migration steps up front.
3) Make it trivial for account teams to localize and personalize messages for enterprise customers.

Audiences and segmentation rules:

- Self-serve (trial/PLG) – short digest, emphasized auto-fallbacks, and no forced action.
- Dedicated customers – scheduled maintenance windows; include throughput/latency SLOs and contact for dedicated on-call.
- Private/VPC customers – pre-upgrade checklist + upgrade window coordination with customer ops and KMS/HSM key rotation notes.

Versioning & channel mapping (how we talk about versions):

- LTS channel: Semver major.minor (e.g., 2.0 LTS). Communications must include LTS duration, security backports policy, and migration benefits (kernel and batching improvements, smaller token cost).
- Rolling channel: described as iterative releases; callouts limited to behavioral changes and opt-in features.
- Backward compatible patch: labeled as patch (2.0.x) with criticality and automatic opt-in statement.

Rollout gates and customer-facing metrics to publish:

- Canary health: 5-minute rolling latency, error-rate, and token-cost delta vs baseline (provide links to the Console canary dashboard).
- Gate thresholds: latency +15% over baseline or error-rate > 0.5% triggers pause and immediate customer comms.
- Progress milestones: Canary (1%), Gradual (1-25%), Ramp (25-100%). Messaging includes percent complete and ETA for next milestone.

Communications artifacts (ready-to-send templates) – samples included below: 

1) Release Digest (email subject & body) – Audience: Dedicated / Private
Subject: Redwood Inference runtime-2.0 LTS rolling to your Dedicated pool on 2026-03-24 (maintenance window)
Body: Hello {account_team},

On 2026-03-24 we will begin staging runtime-2.0 (LTS) to your reserved capacity in region {region} during the maintenance window {window_local_time}. This release brings a 20–35% per-token cost improvement for common token lengths via batching and a new KV cache eviction policy.

What we’ll do:
• Canary at 1% of traffic (automated)
• Monitor latency and errors; pause if any gate breaches occur
• Full ramp contingent on canary success (estimate 3–6 hours)

What you should do:
• Review the pre-upgrade checklist (link) and confirm KMS key rotation windows if applicable
• If you rely on pinned model behavior, open a Support ticket within 24h to request a static pin

Rollback window and contact:
• We maintain an automated rollback window for the first 6 hours after ramp start. If we detect regressions we’ll revert and notify you with a post-rollback summary. For urgent concerns, contact your AM or support@redwood.ai (Priority: Dedicated).

2) Self-serve digest (short) – Audience: PLG
Subject: Minor runtime update (2.0.x) – smoother batching and lower cost
Body: We’re gradually rolling an update to improve performance and reduce costs. No action needed. If you see unusual responses, enable the Console trace and file a ticket.

3) In-app banner copy (for Console)
Banner headline: Scheduled runtime update: 2026-03-24 – Learn more
Banner body: We’re rolling runtime-2.0 (LTS) across regions. Canary monitoring is active; most customers see lower token costs. Read the digest or opt-out of automatic upgrades for this environment.
CTAs: [Read digest] [Opt out] [Open support ticket]

4) Migration checklist (one-pager for customers) – key items:
• Confirm pinned model versions or request pin with Support
• Snapshot/record any custom tokenizer settings or function-tooling expectations
• Validate KMS/HSM availability windows (Private)
• Run your small-sample prompt suite against the canary endpoint (link)
• If embedding vectors are used for indexing, validate embedding model ID and dimension compatibility

5) Post-rollback incident summary template (what customers get if rollback occurs):
• Timeline of events (UTC)
• Observed regression metrics vs baseline
• Root cause (if known) or interim mitigation
• Next steps and estimated timeline to reattempt

Escalation and support playbook for account teams:

- Expected support flow: Tier-1 handles triage with checklist; Tier-2 (runtime) engages for reproducible regressions; Engineering runbook (ENG-7329) to capture kernel-level logs, KV cache diffs, and sample traces.
- SLA promises for Dedicated customers: define 1-hour acknowledgment during maintenance windows and hourly status updates until rollback or resolution.

Localization and personalization guidance:

- Replace region/time placeholders, translate core digest into local languages for large customers, and change technical depth by audience tag ("Engineering contact" vs "Billing/Procurement copy"). Provide a short and a long variant of each message.

Metrics and observability links to include in outgoing messages:

- Console canary dashboard (link)
- Token cost delta widget URL (link)
- Recent regressions log (internal link for AMs)

Owner, dependencies, and artifacts:

- Owner: Product — Marina Santos (assignee).
- Dependencies: ENG runtime rollout automation (ENG-7329), Console banner control API (ENG-18410), and Support runbook updates (PM-21894).
- Artifacts: staging runbook (confluence: /space/Release/runbook-runtime-2.0), sample GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912, canary dashboard: console.redwood.ai/canary/runtime-2.0

Acceptance criteria:

1) Email and Console digest templates available as copy + plain-text + HTML in the shared Drive folder.
2) Segmented templates exist for Self-serve, Dedicated, and Private with localization placeholders.
3) Pre-upgrade checklist and rollback summary templates uploaded and linked from the Console release notes.
4) AM and Support playbooks updated with escalation paths and SLA expectations.
